evidence.observation: Daily retention state machine. Lists projects, filters by owned agents when provided, then per project computes terminalStatus (success/failed/fail), terminalExpired (now - updatedAt >= FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 3 days), restoredExpired (status === 'archived' with restoredAt > 0 and now - restoredAt >= RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS = 24h), and archivedNeedsUnload (archived with restoredAt === 0 and at least one agent still loaded). Only expired-terminal / expired-restored / still-loaded-archived projects are archived; everything else is pushed to skipped/kept. Archived projects whose agents are already unloaded are moved to archived without an RPC (archive is idempotent), otherwise it calls 'wattclaw.team.project.archive'. Returns { scanned, kept, archived, skipped, failed }.

Activation/restore transition. Lists current gateway agents, computes project members missing from that list, and re-creates only those members via 'wattclaw.team.project.member.update' (passing through name/role/soul/skills/richSkills/models). Re-fetches agents.list if any member was restored, then throws if any project agent id is still absent ('WattClaw agents were not restored'). Returns { project, agents, restored }, where restored is true exactly when the incoming project status is 'archived' — this is the archived -> restored signal consumed by the server's markWattClawProjectRestored.

Idempotent ensure/loading transition for a non-archived project. If all desired agent ids are already present in agents.list it returns immediately; otherwise it applies the gateway config (config.get then config.apply, tolerating the expected 'Connection closed' / 'WebSocket not connected' post-apply disconnect), waits pollIntervalMs, then polls agents.list until the deadline (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS 30s, DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 300ms). Throws 'WattClaw agents were not loaded' with the still-missing ids if the timeout elapses. This is the ensure_loaded guard invoked from server/index.js project start.

Schedules the retention sweep at 18:00 Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8) each day: computes 18:00 Shanghai as a UTC instant and rolls forward 24h when that instant is <= now. This is the cron-equivalent trigger for the state machine in pruneWattClawProjectsForUser.

Post-transition ownership registration. For each project member it calls trackAgent(userId, agentId, name, {workspace, description}) and trackSession(userId, 'agent:<id>:main', agentId, project.name, 'main'), returning { agentIds, sessionKeys }. This runs whenever a project is created/started/activated/updated so multi-user isolation keeps the project's agents and sessions owned by the acting user.

File-to-event translation that drives the observed project lifecycle. Reads the watched file (readJsonFile treats ENOENT as missing), skips unchanged content unless force=true, bumps entry.revision. For config.json it publishes 'wattclaw.team.project.deleted' when the file is missing and 'wattclaw.team.project.updated' with { project: value } otherwise. For task-list.json it publishes 'wattclaw.team.tasks.updated' with tasks ([] when missing) and throws if a present task-list is not an array. This is the source of the realtime lifecycle events the frontend store consumes.

Realtime watcher service factory. subscribe(clientId, projectId, tenantId, projectDir) unsubscribes any prior subscription, keys watchers by '<tenant|single>:<projectId>', creates an fs.watch (persistent:false) over the project directory, registers the client, and force-publishes both config.json and task-list.json immediately. Watcher callbacks debounce per-file (default 80ms) via scheduleFile and only react to basename matches in WATCHED_FILES ({config.json, task-list.json}). unsubscribe removes the client and closes the watcher when it was the last one; stop() closes all; getActiveProjectCount exposes the live watcher count.

Resolves the on-disk project directory that the event service watches, validating projectId (and tenantId when present) as safe path segments, then probing container/host data roots, GATEWAY_CONFIG_DIR, /home/wattman/.openclaw and $HOME/.openclaw with the '.wattclaw-team/projects/<id>' suffix, returning the first existing candidate or null. Subscription fails with 503 when this returns null, so it gates whether lifecycle events can be observed at all.

claims.claim: A project has terminal statuses success/failed/fail that are retained for 3 days (FINAL_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS) and then archived by the daily retention sweep, while non-terminal statuses (pending, in_progress) and fresh terminal projects are skipped/kept; 'fail' is treated identically to 'failed'.

An archived project re-enters retention decision-making through access state: once restored (restoredAt > 0) it is re-archived after 24h (RESTORED_PROJECT_RETENTION_MS); if it was never restored (restoredAt === 0) it is archived only while its agents are still loaded on the gateway, and is treated as already-kept when its agents are gone.

Activation is the archived -> restored transition: activateWattClawProjectRuntime re-creates only the project members missing from agents.list via wattclaw.team.project.member.update, re-lists agents, throws if any project agent is still missing, and returns restored === (status === 'archived').
Scheduling is deterministic wall-clock based: nextWattClawRetentionRunAt targets 18:00 Asia/Shanghai every day, rolling to the next day when the candidate instant is not strictly after now.

Every project mutation fans out to per-user ownership tracking: trackWattClawProjectOwnership registers each member agent and its 'agent:<id>:main' session for the acting user, which is what keeps retention and visibility scoped to the correct owner.

Project lifecycle is emitted from disk-file changes: config.json transitions produce wattclaw.team.project.updated (present) or wattclaw.team.project.deleted (missing), and task-list.json produces wattclaw.team.tasks.updated with tasks [] when missing, so the frontend state mirrors the project file rather than an in-memory model.

Realtime observation is subscription-scoped and idempotent: subscribing force-publishes both watched files to the new client immediately, watcher callbacks are debounced per file and filtered to config.json/task-list.json, and the watcher is closed as soon as the last client unsubscribes (getActiveProjectCount returns 0), so no events are emitted after the last unsubscribe.

Event observation is gated on directory resolution: resolveWattClawProjectDirectory validates path segments and probes a fixed candidate list, returning null when the project directory does not exist, which the server maps to a 503 and therefore no lifecycle stream.

The runtime and events services compose into one lifecycle: the runtime decides and performs project state changes (retain/archive/restore/load), and the events service is what surfaces the resulting project file state to clients, so a runtime archive is observable as a config.json-driven 'archived' project.updated.

lifecycle_table.guard: 'fail' normalized to same terminal branch as 'failed'; archive RPC on success, failure recorded in result.failed
restoredAt === 0 and at least one project agent still in agents.list
restoredAt === 0 and no project agent loaded; treated as already unloaded
activateWattClawProjectRuntime re-creates only missing members via member.update, re-lists, throws if any agent still missing

lifecycle_table.trigger: project start when runtime agents not yet loaded
lifecycle_table.guard: if missing agents: config.get + config.apply then poll agents.list until 30s deadline (300ms interval)
basename matches WATCHED_FILES; debounced 80ms; skipped if raw content unchanged unless force
present value must be an array else logged error and no publish; missing publishes tasks: []
force-publishes both config.json and task-list.json to that client only
closes watcher when entry.clients.size === 0; getActiveProjectCount returns 0; no further events

conclusion: WattClaw project lifecycle in these two modules is a file-backed, day-driven state machine. wattclaw-project-runtime.js owns state decisions and transitions: it schedules a daily 18:00 Asia/Shanghai sweep (nextWattClawRetentionRunAt), and pruneWattClawProjectsForUser partitions owned projects into kept/skipped versus archived using three orthogonal expiry rules — terminal success/failed/fail older than 3 days, restored archived projects older than 24h, and cold archived projects whose agents are still loaded. Activation (activateWattClawProjectRuntime) is the archived -> restored edge, re-creating only missing members and reporting restored=true, while ensureWattClawProjectRuntime is the load edge that applies gateway config and polls until all agents are present or a 30s deadline passes; trackWattClawProjectOwnership fans every transition out into per-user agent/session ownership for multi-user isolation. wattclaw-project-events.js is the observation half: it resolves and watches each project's config.json and task-list.json, force-publishes both on subscribe, then translates file writes into wattclaw.team.project.updated, wattclaw.team.project.deleted and wattclaw.team.tasks.updated events (debounced 80ms, per-client subscriptions, watcher closed on last unsubscribe/orphan). Together, runtime decides and applies project state, and events surfaces the resulting project-file state to clients, so an archive performed by retention becomes a config.json-driven 'archived' project.updated on the wire. The lifecycle_table above enumerates the states and transitions; all 16 focused runtime checks passed.

validation.notes: The repository has no test framework installed (node_modules/.bin/vitest absent) and dependency installation is out of scope, so the supplied vitest suites (wattclaw-project-runtime.test.js, wattclaw-project-events.test.js) could not be executed as-is. Instead a dependency-free ESM harness exercised the real modules directly: retention scheduling (18:00 Asia/Shanghai) and the full prune state machine (terminal 3-day expiry for success/failed/fail, 24h restored-archive expiry, cold-archived keep/archive split, ownership filtering), activation restore semantics, and the file-driven event service (subscribe force-publish, project.updated on config change, project.deleted on config removal, watcher close on unsubscribe, directory resolution) using a temporary directory under .prale-eval that is removed afterward. Result: 16/16 checks passed. `node --check` also passed for both source files. The harness file was removed after the run.
